When working on my user space applications
column2: I found a bug in the synthetic

column1: event code where the automated synthetic event field was not matching the
event field calculation it was attached to. Looking deeper into it
because the calculation hist_field was not given a size.
The synthetic event fields are matched to their hist_fields either by
having the field have an identical string type
column2: or if that does not match

column1: then the size and signed values are used to match the fields.
The problem arose when I tried to match a calculation where the fields
were ""unsigned int"". My tool created a synthetic event of type ""u32"". But
it failed to match. The string was:
diff=field1-field2:onmatch(event).trace(synth
Adding debugging into the kernel
column2: I found that the size of ""diff"" was 0.

column1: And since it was given ""unsigned int"" as a type
code used size and signed. The signed matched
column2: but the size of u32 (4) did

column1: not match zero
column2: and the event failed to be created.

column1: This can be worse if the field you want to match is not one of the
acceptable fields for a synthetic event. As event fields can have any type
that is supported in Linux
column2: this can cause an issue. For example

column1: type is an enum. Then there's no way to use that with any calculations.
Have the calculation field simply take on the size of what it is
calculating.
